intro.text: These results come from a census of five accents in prose verses: pashta, segolta, telisha gedolah, telisha qetanna, and zarqa. The printed editions are the Koren Classic Tanakh, Classic Edition, Large Size, and the Feldheim Simanim Tanakh, Elḥanan Yosef edition.

An atom is a written form bounded by spaces or maqaf. A chanted word is one atom or a whole maqaf compound. A stress helper indicates stress within the chanted word. A reading here is counted at the atom that bears the target accent. References use MAM verse numbers and, where useful, the atom's position within that verse.

The census uses the MAM-parsed plus text at commit eba06de1. It compares Koren with MAM’s printed-tradition Decalogues and the Simanim Tanakh with MAM’s manuscript-tradition ones, as the selected comparisons do. The two printed editions give טעם תחתון in their main text and טעם עליון in their appendices. MAM’s printed tradition has 68 readings with the five accents in the Decalogues, and its manuscript tradition has 66.
The selected comparisons, with the printed forms and scans, are on a separate page.

findings.text: For segolta, telisha gedolah, telisha qetanna, and zarqa, each edition has 14 places with the same accent and an additional helper. At 1Sam 17:37, both editions have a zarqa helper on yod of וַיֹּאמֶר֮. At Ezek 13:19, both have a segolta helper on lamed of לֶחֶם֒.

The four Koren grouping differences in the table above are places where the target accent agrees. Three of them are in the Decalogues, at atom 12 of Exod 20:2, Exod 20:9 and Deut 5:6; there Koren agrees with MAM’s printed tradition in accent and helper at all 68 readings with the five accents. At Ezek 31:12, MAM has pashta on בְּכֹל֙ where Koren has a maqaf joining it to the following atom. This exchange counts once, under the accent differences.

At 20 lone-pashta locations, each edition has the primary MAM spelling and the MAM alternative has no corresponding accented form in that edition. At Dan 1:4, both editions have the alef in the primary MAM spelling, while MAM’s spelling alternative כׇּל־מוּם֩ has no separate accented form in either edition.
In the combined reading of Gen 35:22, both editions agree with MAM at all three eligible places. The chanted words are יִשְׂרָאֵל֙, וַיִּשְׁכַּ֕ב֙, and אֶת־בִּלְהָ֖ה֙.

intro.text: Ten of the 42 Koren spelling differences required alignment by letter. At Job 1:10, Koren has the ketiv letters with the qere’s pointing. Both MAM and Koren have the telisha gedolah helper on tav.
